Senator Beebe-Center, Representative HflS6I1fLlS, and distinguished members of the Joint Standing
Committee on Criminal Justice and Public Safety, my name is Chip Curry. I represent Senate District 11, which includes all of the 26 rural, coastal, and island communities of Waldo County. Today, I am introducing LD 768, "An Act to Promote Public Safety and Retain Essential First Responders by Funding
the Maine Length of Service Award Program."

The Maine Length of Service Award Program, or LOSAP, is a retirement benefit program designed to
recognize and retain the volunteer firefighters and EMS p61`SO1`l1'16l who serve as the foundation of
Maine's emergency response system, especially in rural communities like mine. These volunteers
respond to house fires, traffic accidents, medical emergencies, and a wide range of disasters. LOSAP is
a way to say, "We see your service and we value it."

The concept is simple: Each year, a volunteer meets service and training benchmarks, and the state contributes to a retirement account on their behalf. It's a modest yet meaningful benefit designed to encourage retention, boost morale, and recognize the vital role volunteers play in keeping their neighbors
safe.

This idea is not new. The Maine Fire Protection Services Commission first began developing LOSAP in 2003. The Legislature formally established the program in 2015 with the passage of LD 164 in the 127th

Now, LD 768 picks up where LD 588 left off. It proposes $2.5 million in ongoing General Fund
appropriations in each year of the biennium to support this essential program. With LOSAP, we are offering a modest but meaningful retirement benefit to the Mainers who serve their communities as
volunteer firefighters and emergency medical p61`SOI1I16l.
These are not symbolic roles. They are frontline responders who put their lives on the line. In rural
Maine, especially, our emergency services often depend entirely on volunteers. Without adequate
support, we risk losing these community pillars to burnout, financial hardship, or other obligations.
As we face growing challenges in recruiting and retaining first responders, LOSAP offers a powerful
tool to help towns sustain vital services. It also sends a clear message: that we recognize and value the service of those who protect our neighbors, our homes, and our communities.
I respectfully urge the committee to support LD 768 and help us fulfill the promise of LOSAP once and for all. Thank you for your time. I'm happy to answer any questions you may have.

Maine Length of Service Award Program

April 23, 2025

Good Morning Senator Beebe-Center, Representative Hasenfus, and honorable members of the Committee
on Criminal Justice and Public Safety. My name is Frederick Brewer, and I am the Governors Appointee to the Length of Service Award Program for the State of Maine. l was appointed to the LOSAP board because of my background as a CPA, my training and expertise working with municipalities and retirement plans & my life
long experience as a fourth-generation volunteer firefighter on the Massasoit Engine Co. of Damariscotta. i appreciate the opportunity to speak in support of LD 786, An Act To Promote Public Safety and Retain Essential First Responders by Funding the Maine Length of Service Award Program. The original bill that
established the program was passed under the 127"` legislative session in 2015. We have actively been
working toward funding this bill since that time. Funding for the program was provided from the
Appropriations Committee in the 130"` legislative session with startup money of $500,000. We have been
working to establish the program over the last three years and are now accepting municipal contributions to
the program. We submitted a request for $2.5 million in funding in the Biennial Budget the Appropriations
Committee is currently reviewing. Unfortunately the funds we requested as part of the regular budgetary
process were cut out of the budget that was submitted under LD 210. This has shifted our focus from implementing the program and getting participants enrolled in the program to asking your committee to approve our request for funding.
This bill is the product of an effort to address Maine's crisis to attract, retain, and support our volunteer first responders, which our communities have been so reliant upon for generations and even more acutely today. This bill seeks to provide funding for Maine's LOSAP:
The first part of the funding will appropriate funds for the administrative costs of the program so that
municipalities in Maine can contribute to the program for the benefit of their volunteer firefighters and EMS
personnel.
The second part of the funding is for a State contribution to the program. The State appropriation will fund
contributions for firefighters and EMS personnel that meet the training, meeting attendance, and calls that
their department has during the year. This is referred to as qualified services under the plan.
The LOSAP board established the service award calculation so that first responders can accrue benefits for services that will benefit the communities they serve the most. The benefit of the state contribution is that
we have set a floor of 30 points that the participant needs to earn. lf they do not achieve the 30 points, then
they will not receive a contribution from the State. The ceiling of the program is $1,000 annually per participant. This enables departments to encourage additional participation from their membership by
showing them how much service credit they have earned throughout the year. The communities that benefit the most from this program, are those in the more rural part ofthe State.
Maine's LOSAP is a deferred compensation program under internal Revenue Code 457. A defined
contribution program puts funds in the participants account and they can draw on it after they reach retirement age and have provided 5 years of vesting service to their community. The defined contribution plan is effective because it doesn't create any pension liabilities that the State will have to fund in future

years. The only funding requirement is the annual contribution to the program based on the participants service to their community.
LOSAP programs vary from State to State. States like Maryland, Wisconsin, Oregon and Pennsylvania have
similar State-wide, defined contribution programs. States like New York, New Mexico, Montana have
defined benefit programs that provide a specific pension amount, when they reach retirement age, based on their years of service. Some States like New York allow the individual volunteer departments to have their own LOSAP program that is monitored by the State. Maine is a State wide program that allows individual
municipalities to add to the first responders account to supplement the contribution from the State, as they see fit.
For the sake of the health and future of our volunteer first responders in Maine, and the communities that depend on them, I urge you to vote in favor of this bill. I welcome any questions about the operation ofthe program and thank you for your service.

Senator Beebe-Center, Representative Hasenfus, and Distinguished Members of the Joint Standing Committee on Criminal Justice and Public Safety,
My name is William Gillespie, and I serve as the Fire Chief for the Town of Liberty, Maine. Additionally, I am writing to you today in my capacity as President and Legislative Liaison for the Maine Fire Chiefs Association, an organization representing over 400 Fire Chiefs across the state.
This letter conveys the strong support of the Maine Fire Chiefs Association for LD 786, An Act to Promote Public Safety and Retain Essential First Responders by Funding the Maine Length of Service Award Program.
We extend our sincere gratitude to Senator Curry for sponsoring this crucial legislation, which seeks to support the dedicated Fire and EMS personnel who provide invaluable services to our communities throughout Maine.
Since its inception in 2017, the Maine Length of Service Award Program (LOSAP) Board of Directors has worked diligently to establish a sustainable program. Beginning in 2018, the Board consistently presented legislative requests for the necessary support to bring this vital initiative to fruition. The $500,000 funding allocated during the 131st Legislative Session was instrumental in enabling the Board to contract with a third-party administrator to manage the program effectively. Currently, the LOSAP program has successfully enrolled 600 members, with over $90,000 in municipal contributions secured. Due to the statutory requirements and operational framework established for this program, we are currently in the third year of a five-year contractual agreement, necessitating continued financial support to meet our obligations. The non-lapsing nature of previous funding has been critical in allowing us to strategically plan and now request further investment to ensure the program's long-term viability. As the Maine Length of Service Award Program is in its initial stages of implementation, we respectfully urge your continued support in our efforts to retain and reward the dedicated first responders who have committed years of outstanding service to our state. Therefore, I respectfully request your favorable consideration of and support for LD 786.
